title: A method for isolating RNA from canine bone
author: Rebecca Nance
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf9vjr66

steps.title: Remove soft tissue and periosteum
steps.instruction: Remove all exterior soft tissue around the diaphysis using scissors, scalpel, and KimWipes; scrape the bone along the diaphysis exterior with a scalpel to completely remove periosteum, ensuring removal of contaminating exterior tissues.

steps.title: Discard epiphyses
steps.instruction: Cut off and discard the epiphyses with large bolt cutters, taking care not to disturb the tubular structure of the diaphysis.

steps.title: Centrifuge diaphysis to collect marrow
steps.instruction: Place the diaphysis in a 1.7 mL microfuge tube and centrifuge at 10,000 × g, room temperature, for 10 min. The liquid collected at the bottom is bone marrow/fat.

steps.title: PBS washes of diaphysis
steps.instruction: Transfer the diaphysis to a new 1.7 mL tube, add 1× PBS enough to completely cover the bone, and centrifuge at 10,000 × g, room temperature, for 5 min. Repeat the transfer, add fresh 1× PBS to cover, and centrifuge again at 10,000 × g, room temperature, for 5 min.

steps.title: Snap‑freeze and store bone
steps.instruction: Snap‑freeze the bone in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C for up to 8 months until RNA extraction.

steps.title: Prepare Tri‑Reagent tubes with beads
steps.instruction: Prepare two 1.7 mL Eppendorf Safe‑Lock tubes; add 1 mL Tri‑Reagent and approximately 0.5 g zirconium oxide beads (0.5 mm diameter) to each tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Grind bone to fine powder
steps.instruction: Grind the frozen bone into a fine powder using a RNase‑free steel mortar and pestle on dry ice, working quickly to avoid RNase degradation. Mortar and pestle may be RNase‑free by wiping with RNase Away, wrapping in aluminum foil, and baking at 350 °F for 6 h or overnight, then freezing at –80 °C before use.

steps.title: Divide powder into reagent tubes
steps.instruction: Divide the bone powder equally between the two prepared tubes containing Tri‑Reagent and beads.

steps.title: Homogenize with Bullet Blender
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a Bullet Blender set to speed 5.5 and run 4 cycles of 30 s homogenization followed by 1 min incubation on ice between cycles.

steps.title: Incubate homogenate at room temperature
steps.instruction: Incubate the homogenized samples at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Add bromochloropropane and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL bromochloropropane (BCP) to each tube, vortex thoroughly, and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.

steps.title: Phase separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 20,000 × g, 4 °C, for 15 min.

steps.title: Add DNase I to aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the top aqueous layer, add 10 µL DNase I and 1/10 volume DNase I Reaction Buffer, and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Inactivate DNase with EDTA heat
steps.instruction: Inactivate DNase by adding 10 µL of 25 mM EDTA (included) and heat the mixture at 65 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Add ethanol and mix
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 70 % ethanol to the sample and mix well by pipetting.

steps.title: Bind RNA to RNeasy column
steps.instruction: Transfer the mixture to an RNeasy Micro Kit column placed in a 2 mL collection tube and centrifuge at 21,000 × g, room temperature, for 1 min.

steps.title: Wash column with Buffer RW1
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, add 700 µL Buffer RW1 to the column, incubate on the column for 2 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at 21,000 × g, room temperature, for 1 min.

steps.title: Wash column with Buffer RPE
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, add 500 µL Buffer RPE, incubate on the column for 2 min at room temperature, and centrifuge at 21,000 × g, room temperature, for 1 min.

steps.title: Wash column with 80% ethanol
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, add 500 µL 80 % ethanol, incubate on the column for 2 min at room temperature, and centrifuge at 21,000 × g, room temperature, for 3 min.

steps.title: Dry column and prepare for elution
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, replace the 2 mL collection tube with a fresh one, and centrifuge the column at 21,000 × g (temperature not specified) for 5 min with the lid open to dry the membrane.

steps.title: Elute RNA with RNase‑free water
steps.instruction: Add 17 µL RNase‑free water pre‑heated to 65 °C to the column, incubate on the column for 10 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at 21,000 × g, room temperature, for 5 min to elute RNA.

steps.title: Measure RNA concentration and purity
steps.instruction: Determine RNA concentration and purity using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.
